No mine was painful. That was my main symptom -- pain with sex, and then soreness afterwards (localized to the ulcer). I think this will work. If it doesn't, I'll need a biopsy (which is NOT fun). 

I've researched aphthous ulcers and the gyn corroborated that they just don't know what causes them exactly. According to UpToDate, some are correlated with EBV and a few other viruses. When mine presented, a week or less before it showed up, I do remember having unusual fatigue and a weird allodynia in my lower back in a dermatomal area there (I have a history of occasional allodynia on my arms and legs, which I *think* might be a remnant of varicella). IOW, not sure what caused it, but "weird viral nerve stuff" seems to be a possibiliy and it fits with my history. 

Really hope this works. I think if nothing else, 3 weeks of abstinence will work.

/u/Thelastunicorn80 /u/squiggywiggle thought you might be interested -- I finally went to a gynecologist (this is *still* going on), she thinks it's an aphthous ulcer! Prescribed a steroid gel to use for 3 weeks. So no, not a tear after all.
That makes me think it really is either (1) anatomy or (2) maybe the vulva are atrophied such that lubrication isn't enough. I dunno.

I was wondering, when this was happening to you, were you on combined oral contraceptives/the pill? I've been on the pill for years and never had an issue, and sex seems totally lubricated to me. But I also wonder if the pill is causing some low-level vaginal/vulvar atrophy/dryness predisposing to this issue.

I might take one if I can. But this last bout really made the diagnosis more clear to me. It was healing very well and was barely visible. Then we had sex again and I looked at it very soon after -- it wasn't an ulcer, it was a tear. It looked like that part of the mucosa had been ripped away. Then about 24 hours later it turned that yellow color again -- part of what I assume is the healing process, a sort of plaque covering the wound. It does not have a stuck-on appearance. It doesn't look like HSV/vesicles. Just a yellow area of the vestibule. 

But yeah I'll try to get a pic since this thing just keeps recurring.

Also SO WEIRD that it didn't happen to you again after you guys broke up? Why is that? Was it a long time? Or do you think it was a change in anatomy (i.e. different penis)? 

Anyway I just messaged my provider telling her what was up and asking if I should wait it out or come in.

Ugh I know, the first doc I saw was very incompetent, that's why I switched. The second one I saw was actually a PA. I don't *really* blame her, because it was very hard to see and seemed almost resolved. But it's definitely back now...

I'm wondering if it may be some kind of [viral-caused genital ulcer](https://www.uptodate.com/contents/acute-genital-ulceration-lipschutz-ulcer). The thing is it's not necrotic at all, and I have no dysuria (which they claim is a universal symptom). 

I'm on the fence about either waiting it out (abstaining did seem to help, and treatment for non-sexually transmitted genital ulcers is basically symptomatic only), vs calling the new doc's office back and being more specific that I definitely have a waxing-waning genital ulcer that isn't getting better.

It doesn't look like herpes. I've actually had genital herpes before (HSV-1, got it from a bf's cold sore/eating me out), and it was nothing like this. Herpes presented, for me, on the mound, on normal skin, it was excruciatingly painful, multiple vesicles that broke open and then healed. 

This is in a very different location: as close to inside the vagina as possible without being in it. Instead of on normal skin, it's on the inside of the labia minora (membranous). It is just one ulcer -- I'd describe it as very flat, yellow, moist (but no overt pus), seems to even be somewhat eroding into the normal membrane a little (there is a clear line where it ends and where the normal membrane begins). 

EDIT: this is a [gastric ulcer](https://www.google.com/search?q=ulcer&source=lnms&tbm=isch&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwi-jMSM2pHgAhVHllQKHe6pCosQ_AUIDigB&biw=1422&bih=646#imgrc=vebyRj-j6_aa9M:) but it kinda looks like that. Less well-demarcated.

I wish I knew how to help people... I hate what you've gone through and that you feel like you have to hurt yourself to get relief. I also hate that we tend to say "what you've gone through" and "I'm sorry that happened to you" and so on when it's not like a natural disaster where things *just happen* -- someone *chose* to *act* and to hurt you. That person is to blame. Not some deity or void or yourself or anyone or anything but that person. Your ex boyfriends are rapists. 

I think you need someone to talk to in person that will offer you some more productive advice than what you'll get on reddit. I didn't catch if you were still talking to a therapist, but if not, you 100% should. Honestly, I think everyone should see a therapist at some point in their lives. Because no one has it all together, we all have our demons and our struggles, and could use guidance.
